subject: Capacity handshake for Strata AI — preemptible headroom and surge schedule
messages:
From: Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@strata.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai; laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@strata.ai
Date: 2028-11-22T09:05:12-08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity: anticipated surge window for model launch

Tessa / Laura,

We have an internal deadline for our generative search launch on 2029-01-10. Traffic estimates show a sharp spike in the first 72 hours post-launch (~6x baseline) and sustained 2x traffic for ~3 weeks.

We'd like Redwood to support an automatic surge plan and a documented fall-back if our priority jobs exceed reserved capacity. Key asks:
- Can you confirm short-duration preemptible headroom and how eviction would be handled?
- Network and egress limits we should expect during the spike.
- A clear mutual action plan & timeline so our procurement can complete the PO.

Jacob Lee
CRO, Strata AI
jacob.lee@strata.ai
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@strata.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-22T11:48:03-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: anticipated surge window for model launch

Jacob — thanks for the clear signal. High level response below; Ben and Karthik are looped for sizing and policy details.

Plan (summary):
- Short bursts: we can grant preemptible headroom for up to 48 hours at 3x reserved capacity, subject to queued-priority limits.
- Eviction model: preemptible jobs are last-in-first-out; we guarantee graceful eviction hooks (SIGHUP + 60s drain) for graceful checkpointing.
- Fallback: automatic model downgrade to a smaller quantized variant if headroom is exhausted; manual failover to another region if desired.

Please find a draft mutual action plan in the attached sizing spreadsheet. I propose a technical kickoff the week of 11/28 to lock SLAs and finalize procurement path.

Attachments: [Attachment: dedicated-sizing-spreadsheet.xlsx (xlsx, 320KB)]

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Strategic Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0123
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai; karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@strata.ai>
Date: 2028-11-23T08:22:45-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: anticipated surge window for model launch

Tessa / team — I took Jacob's traffic numbers and sketched a capacity plan. See bullets below (numbers are conservative; full calculations in the spreadsheet).

Sizing highlights:
- Baseline reserved pool: 12 A100-equivalent GPUs (customer commit).
- Short burst headroom: allow up to +36 GPUs (3x baseline) for windows up to 48 hours.
- Sustained uplift: maintain +12 GPUs for up to 21 days (2x baseline), using reserved+ephemeral mix to control cost.

Operational guardrails (practical):
- Preemptible eviction priority: non-critical background jobs -> batch jobs -> interactive latency-sensitive inference (protected by token-based priority).
- Minimum preemptible time slice: 10s to allow KV cache persistence; eviction will attempt to move warm KV to persistent cache first.
- Billing: preemptible CPU/GPU units will be billed at a discounted rate; credits for involuntary evictions negotiated in SOW.

I've attached the spreadsheet with per-model GPU hours, expected token throughput, and recommended slab sizing.

[Attachment: dedicated-sizing-spreadsheet.xlsx (xlsx, 320KB)]

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Dedicated Capacity Planning | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai; tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai; Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@strata.ai>
Date: 2028-11-24T10:31:10-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: anticipated surge window for model launch

Adding the autoscale policy draft and network constraints. Key points for the kickoff doc:

Autoscale thresholds (proposal):
- Scale-up: if 1-min p95 latency > 450ms OR queued requests > 120 for > 60s, add one GPU slab (8 GPUs) up to preemptible headroom cap.
- Scale-down: reduce when 5-min p95 latency < 250ms AND queued requests < 40 for > 300s.
- Warm start: keep 1 "shoulder" slab warm during business hours to minimize cold-start impact for realtime endpoints.

Eviction and grace:
- Eviction signal sent 60s before termination; SDK exposes graceful checkpoint API.
- Model fallback policies: automatic downgrade path per endpoint, configurable per-route.

Network & egress notes:
- Recommend a 10Gbps per-GPU north-south egress budget during spikes; application-level rate-limiting recommended for vector-search fanouts.
- If Strata wants cross-region failover, we should negotiate multi-region replication for KV caches; this adds ~5–8s failover latency.

Attachment: [Attachment: network-requirements.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]

I'll fold this into the kickoff deck. Kicks off 11/28 works for me.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
